sense: for a phone or a battery

terms.comment: Our formation, from replēre, our word for charging, with the suffix of instruments: arātrum, rāstrum, and from a verb in -ēre fulgētrum (Lewis & Short). It pairs with Traupman’s accumulātrum: the replētrum fills the accumulātrum. No reference work has a word for a charger.

terms.grammar: phrase: the dative of purpose with a gerundive
terms.comment: The same thing spelled out, for a first mention to someone who does not know the word.

sources: Lewis & Short: repleo · Lewis & Short: fulgetrum · Lewis & Short: instrumentum
No source has a Latin word for a charger; the word is built on our word for charging (see “charge”).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
